title: Very few species of past periods have living descendants

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Very few species of past periods have living descendants

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Like a tree in which only a few early twigs grew into surviving branches, very few of the species that lived in long-past geological periods now have living modified descendants, and many whole orders, families and genera have died out entirely.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Of the many twigs which flourished when the tree was a mere bush, only two or three, now grown into great branches, yet survive and bear all the other branches; so with the species which lived during long-past geological periods, very few now have living and modified descendants.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IV, “Natural Selection”; section “Summary”. Scope: all lineages over geological time

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch04-26: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Extinction and survival patterns can be estimated for well-sampled clades. Existing data cannot directly identify descendants for most ancient species or accurately enumerate all past diversity.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For clades with fossil-calibrated trees, estimate the fraction of past species or lineages with extant descendants and count complete extinction of higher taxa. A small surviving fraction and many wholly extinct clades support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The denominator of all species that lived is unknown because fossil sampling is incomplete.

Most fossil species cannot be assigned as direct ancestors.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Extinction of orders, families, and genera is directly countable by joining the fossil record to a living checklist, and that half of the statement is within reach of a standard analysis. Whether a particular ancient species has living modified descendants is usually unknowable and is proxied by survival of its higher taxon. The qualitative scarcity of surviving deep-time lineages is robust in well-sampled groups, but it is not a species-by-species resolution of the full tree.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Join fossil occurrences in deep time bins to living checklists and phylogenies, and compute the fraction of species, genera, families, and orders with any living descendant lineage. A very small species fraction and a large number of wholly extinct higher taxa would confirm the claim; survival of a large share of ancient species-lineages, or rarity of higher-taxon extinction, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Species-level ancestor-descendant links are almost never resolved, so higher taxa stand in for them.

The fossil record samples a biased subset of past species.

Extinct names can hide surviving lineages that were reclassified.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.68
data existence: 0.86
data adequacy: 0.58
analysis feasibility: 0.76
discriminating power: 0.6
